title: handshake-evidence-stitching-and-approval-latency-sim
content:
Context and intent:

This is a working PRD sketch for an experimental compact evidence "stitching" model and accompanying approval-latency simulation harness for customer-managed networking handshakes. Goal is to produce an operator-friendly evidence ledger (compact, queryable, tamper-evident) that can be emitted during VPC handshakes and used by approval gates with predictable latency budgets.

Why this matters (problem statement):
- Customers with private deployments demand minimal, auditable proof that a network handshake (peer, route, connector) was accepted and enacted.
- Current approval flow emits verbose syslog/pcap-level telemetry that is heavy to store and slow to validate for downstream audits.
- Product needs a lightweight evidence model that preserves forensic value (who approved, what changed, pre/post diff) while keeping approval latency within SLOs (target: <= 1200ms median for acceptance path).

High-level proposal: evidence-stitcher + latency-sim harness
- Evidence-Stitcher: an agent-side library (customer-edge shim or operator sidecar) that aggregates discrete signals generated during the handshake (auth token fingerprint, config diff hash, operator-assertion, time-stamps, route fingerprints) into a compact signed bundle (jsonld-ish, compressed, signature).
- Decision-Ledger API: an immutable append-only endpoint (on control plane or self-hosted lightweight ledger) that accepts bundles and returns a short receipt (receipt id + timing). Receipts used by approval gates and stored in compressed archive for audits.
- Latency Simulation harness: a test runner that injects synthetic handshake traces (from light to heavy) to measure end-to-end approval latency under a configured set of constraints: network RTT, operator approval delay, signature verification cost, ledger write throughput. Generates SLA projections for different customer scaling classes.

Design constraints and non-goals:
- Compactness: target evidence bundles < 2KB uncompressed for typical handshake.
- Verifiability: must include verifiable signatures from operator and the customer edge (HMAC or ECDSA depending on KMS availability).
- Privacy: no raw payload/pkts included — include hashes only and optional blinded metadata.
- Non-goal: this is NOT a replacement for full SYSLOG export or full PCAP forensic capture; it's a concise proof artifact for audits and fast query.

Event model (rough):
- events collected per handshake:
  - handshake.start {ts, session_id, initiator, target, proto_version}
  - auth.challenge {ts, session_id, token_fingerprint}
  - config.apply {ts, session_id, config_hash, diff_summary}
  - operator.approve {ts, session_id, operator_id, approval_type}
  - handshake.end {ts, session_id, result}
- Stitching: evidence-stitcher consumes the event stream for session_id window and produces:
  - bundle {session_id, start_ts, end_ts, participants, hash_chain: [h1,h2..], compact_diff, signatures: [customer_sig, operator_sig], meta: {sampled_metrics}}

Bundle format (compact, human-readable fields):
- session_id: short uuid v7
- timeline: start_ts|end_ts
- participants: [customer_edge_id, operator_id]
- compact_diff: base64url(serialized protobuf diff) OR json compressed with zlib then base64
- hash_chain: list of sha256 hex strings for each event, included in chronological order
- signatures: base64url of ECDSA over canonicalized bundle 
- receipt: assigned by ledger after write, includes write_ts and an incremental sequence number

Risk/Threat modeling notes (quick):
- Replay: mitigate using timestamps + nonces + sequence numbers.
- Tamper: store bundles and ledger receipts in append-only storage with periodic verifiable checkpoints (hash of latest seq).
- Privacy leakage: avoid including IP/payload; only include hashed route descriptors.
- KMS complexity: have two codepaths, HSM-backed signing (enterprise) and ephemeral key HMAC (self-host) with clear UX differences.

Ledger contract (minimal):
- POST /v1/decision-ledger/bundles -> {bundle, signature, origin} returns {receipt_id, write_ts, seq}
- GET /v1/decision-ledger/receipts/{receipt_id} -> {bundle_ref, write_ts, verification_status}
- Query by session_id and time-range for audit viewer

Approval gate integration points:
- Pre-accept: control-plane receives bundle+receipt synchronously before committing route (blocking path). This keeps proof attached to change.
- Post-accept: asynchronous write for non-blocking path, with fallback SLO (if no receipt within threshold, change is rolled back or flagged).
- UX knobs: blocking_threshold_ms (customer can set) and fallback_policy (auto-rollback | staged-accept | allow-with-warning).

Latency simulation plan (experiment):
- Build harness that can run N parallel simulated handshakes with randomized event delays and operator approval distributions (0-5s typical).
- Parameters to sweep: network latency (10ms, 50ms, 200ms), ledger backend (local sqlite, distributed WAL), signature scheme (ECDSA vs HMAC), bundle size distribution (0.5KB, 1KB, 3KB), operator approval delay (auto=0ms, fast human=200-800ms, slow=2-5s).
- Metrics to collect: median and p95 approval-latency end-to-end, ledger write throughput, verification CPU cost per bundle, incidence of rollback triggered by approval SLO miss.
- Acceptance guardrails: target <=1200ms median and <=3000ms p95 for the default blocking policy in Hosted and Dedicated tiers (Private may tolerate higher p95 but should be configurable).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should the ledger be part of the private control plane (customer-managed) or offered as a Redwood-managed inert append endpoint? Hybrid? (privacy vs operational burden)
- Signature UX: how to provision edge keys securely in on-prem installs without user friction? Provide a bootstrap CLI and rotate-on-first-use pattern?
- Query cost: we need a compact audit viewer; do we accept offloading full replay to customer (S3) with index in ledger?
- Sampling vs full retention: for very chatty environments, do we sample bundles and retain full telemetry separately? How to prove sampled representativeness?

Acceptance criteria for MVP:
- PoC evidence-stitcher written in Go + small shim for Debian 11 package install.
- Decision-ledger endpoint (local deploy) capable of 1000 writes/min with <250ms median write latency on small instance.
- Sim harness runs 10k synthetic handshakes and outputs SLA projections and cost estimates.
- Draft of operator UX and rollback policy documented in Confluence (linked).

Next steps (short-term):
- Engineering spike: build minimal bundle encoder and ECDSA signer (2w)
- Sim prototype: port existing traffic-sim to support bundle/ledger model (1w)
- Security review: threat model pass (1w)
- Product: draft customer-facing proposal + privacy SLA alternative (1w)
- Stakeholder sync scheduled: Nov 13 2025 (internal) to review initial spike results

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Talk to infra about append-only store options (immutable S3 vs postgres WAL + periodic checkpointing) — @Marta
- Get KMS onboarding checklist from SRE — @Evan
- Add example bundle with real-looking diffs to this doc (small sample) — follow-up

References & artifacts:
- Confluence: handshake-evidence-playbook (link in top)
- Experiment ticket: JIRA-PRIV-712 (simulate ledger at scale)
- Proto sketch: github.com/redwood-inference/private-onprem/handshake-sim

Unresolved items to surface for review meeting:
- Default blocking policy for Private customers and acceptable p95 latency
- Whether to require operator signature for auto-approved changes (adds latency)
- How to represent config diffs compactly across vendor router platforms (BGP vs VPN vs ALB)

End of draft — comments welcome.
